structures1.name: single jersey
structures1.note: every needle knits on the front bed

structures1.name: reverse jersey
structures1.note: every needle knits on the back bed

structures1.name: 1 × 1 rib
structures1.note: front and back needles alternate; pulls in across

structures1.name: 2 × 2 rib
structures1.note: pairs of front and back needles

structures1.name: garter (purl)
structures1.note: each course changes bed by a transfer; ridges, pulls in along

structures1.name: seed
structures1.note: face and back stitches alternate both ways

structures1.name: tubular
structures1.note: front and back beds in turn: two layers joined at the edges

structures1.name: tuck moss
structures1.note: every other stitch tucks, offset each pass: thick, wide, puckered

structures1.name: tuck honeycomb
structures1.note: double tucks, offset: raised cells; wider and shorter

structures1.name: float stripes
structures1.note: floats behind every other pass; pulls in

structures1.name: eyelets
structures1.note: a loop moved right leaves an empty needle: a hole

structures1.name: hold (short rows)
structures1.note: the needles knit nothing here; the rest grows longer

structures2.name: double knit, YG1 face
structures2.note: YG1 on the front bed, YG2 on the back

structures2.name: double knit, YG2 face
structures2.note: YG2 on the front bed, YG1 on the back

structures2.name: mixed (birdseye)
structures2.note: the two yarns alternate on the face

structures2.name: tuck pair
structures2.note: both guides tuck, one on each bed

structures2.name: YG1 alone
structures2.note: YG1 knits the front, YG2 floats (provisional colour)
